title: 19.9 An 11-to-16.4GHz, 3.4GHz/µs-Slope, 5.32GHz-Chirp-Bandwidth, 0.043%-RMS-Frequency-Error FMCW Digital PLL with Posterior-Segment DPD Featuring 5-Chirp-Cycle Convergence Time
problem: FMCW radars for autonomous driving and IoT require wide-bandwidth chirps with high linearity and fast convergence to multiple frequency bands; multi-vehicle interference and multi-mode operation demand rapid frequency-hopping and DPD convergence within single chirp bursts.
motivation: Autonomous driving and IoT radar applications need frequency-agile FMCW systems that quickly adapt to new bands and handle interference; faster convergence enables more efficient multi-mode radar operation.
method: This system uses a digital phase-locked loop (a feedback circuit that automatically adjusts an oscillator to match a target frequency) to generate frequency sweeps called chirps from 11 to 16.4 GHz. It applies digital predistortion specifically to the final segment of each sweep to pre-correct for hardware distortions, allowing the system to converge—reaching stable operation—within just 5 chirp cycles. The resulting chirps sweep upward at 3.4 GHz per microsecond, cover 5.32 GHz of bandwidth, and maintain 0.043% RMS frequency accuracy despite the hardware's inherent nonlinearities.
key_novelty: Posterior-segment digital predistortion (applying correction only to the end of each frequency sweep rather than throughout) enables convergence within 5 chirp cycles, supporting rapid frequency-switching and multi-mode operation when multiple vehicles share radar spectrum.
